done.why: Every route beyond the troll room was blocked as unfinished: the east passage, the west hole and the south crawlway. The trap door closed behind me, so I couldn't go back up.

about: A small Zork-style start. You enter a white house through a window, collect a lantern, a sword and a sack, then go down a trap door to a cellar and a troll. The deeper caverns are marked as unfinished or suspended.

ending.what: No ending. The accessible area ended at dead-end notes about excavation being suspended.

moments.note: Moving the rug revealed the trap door, a familiar classic beat.
The sword glowed blue near the cellar and brighter at the troll.
The troll fight resolved in a few exchanges, ending with the black fog.
The east passage was unfinished and I couldn't take the pick.
The south crawlway also dead-ended, with a plaque saying excavation was suspended.
'take lantern and sword' failed with 'You can't see any such thing.'

wished: To go further underground into the caverns the title promises.
To take the pick and dig.
To go back up and explore the rest of the house, such as the attic, upstairs and the trophy case.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. Someone has left a pick leaning against the rock, and a note: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: A witty way to say the area is closed.

lines.line: Almost as soon as the troll breathes his last breath, a cloud of sinister black fog envelops him...

fun.why: The classic opening and the troll fight were fun, but there was very little to do.

engagement.why: My interest dropped quickly once every exit turned out to be blocked.

difficulty.why: The troll fell in a few blows and there were no puzzles to solve.

interestingness.why: It was familiar ground with a few fun touches, such as the sword glow and the Management notes.

prose.why: The prose was crisp and in the classic style, and the dead ends were written with humor.
